# Overview

Males have stable isotope values (δ¹³C, δ¹⁵N) and standard length, but no
tracking or diving data. This script asks the same questions as the female
analyses, with methods suited to those data. It replaces
`NESE_NicheWidth_PostBreeding_Males.Rmd`, `NESE_NicheWidth_Males_PB.Rmd` and
`NESE_MaleRepeatabilityIsotopes.Rmd`.

1. **Are there discrete isotopic groups?** Gaussian mixture models with
   correlated isotopes (1–4 groups, including "no groups"), a bootstrap
   likelihood-ratio test, and a null-model test of cluster structure.
2. **The isotopic gradient.** Each male's position along the main axis of
   isotopic variation.
3. **What explains isotopic position?** Standard length, trip type and year.
   Length is tested as an explanation rather than used to define groups.
4. **Isotopic niche.** Niche size and directional overlap of males compared
   with each female strategy (nicheROVER and SIBER), with a sensitivity
   analysis restricted to females sampled in the same years as males.
5. **Repeatability.** Population-level repeatability and within-male
   differences compared with differences between males sampled in the same
   years (exploratory: few repeat males).

**Why the previous approach was replaced.** Clustering on δ¹³C, δ¹⁵N and
length made groups partly size classes; `na.omit()` removed the males without
length, leaving 13 post-breeding males for three clusters; isotopic niches of
clusters defined by the same isotopes overlap little by construction; niches
were estimated in three dimensions from 3–7 males with an unseeded random prior;
and the repeatability script shared the problems of the female version
(per-individual index, mislabelled IDs, hard-coded rows).

**Run first:** `NESE_PB_ForagingStrategies.Rmd` and
`NESE_PM_ForagingStrategies.Rmd` (female strategies, for the sex comparison).

```{r libraries}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(cluster)      # silhouette
library(nicheROVER)
library(rptR)
library(lme4)
# mclust and MASS are called with :: (attaching them masks dplyr functions)
```

# Settings

```{r settings}
SEED <- 20261105
set.seed(SEED)

META_FILE <- "../data/IsotopesDatasetForLuis_2023_4_4.csv"
PB_ASSIGN <- "../results/PB_strategies/A_strategy_assignments.csv"
PM_ASSIGN <- "../results/PM_strategies/A_strategy_assignments.csv"

N_BOOT_LRT <- 999    # bootstrap replicates for the mixture-model LRT
N_NULL     <- 500    # simulations for the cluster-structure null model
N_PERM     <- 9999   # permutations
N_POST     <- 1e4    # nicheROVER posterior draws
N_RPT_BOOT <- 1000   # rptR bootstrap replicates
```

## Helper functions

```{r helpers}
pick1 <- function(x) x[sample.int(length(x), 1)]

# Ward + k-means consolidation (as FactoMineR::HCPC)
hcpc_lite <- function(S, k) {
  cl  <- cutree(hclust(dist(S), method = "ward.D2"), k)
  cen <- apply(S, 2, function(x) tapply(x, cl, mean))
  tryCatch(kmeans(S, centers = cen, iter.max = 100)$cluster, error = function(e) cl)
}

# Freedman-Lane permutation F test for `term`, adjusting for `covars`
fl_test <- function(d, response, term, covars = character(0), B = N_PERM) {
  v  <- c(response, term, covars)
  d  <- d[complete.cases(d[v]), v, drop = FALSE]
  X0 <- model.matrix(reformulate(if (length(covars)) covars else "1"), d)
  X1 <- model.matrix(reformulate(c(covars, term)), d)
  y  <- d[[response]]
  Fstat <- function(y) {
    m0 <- lm.fit(X0, y); m1 <- lm.fit(X1, y)
    r0 <- sum(m0$residuals^2); r1 <- sum(m1$residuals^2)
    ((r0 - r1) / (m1$rank - m0$rank)) / (r1 / (nrow(X1) - m1$rank))
  }
  F_obs <- Fstat(y)
  m0 <- lm.fit(X0, y); fit0 <- y - m0$residuals
  F_p <- replicate(B, Fstat(fit0 + sample(m0$residuals)))
  data.frame(response = response, term = term,
             covariates = if (length(covars)) paste(covars, collapse = " + ") else "none",
             n = nrow(d), F = F_obs, p_perm = (1 + sum(F_p >= F_obs)) / (B + 1))
}

# rptR without progress bars, and results read from its printed summary
fit_rpt <- function(...) { out <- NULL; invisible(capture.output(out <- rpt(...))); out }
rpt_parse <- function(r, comp) {
  txt <- capture.output(print(summary(r)))
  i <- grep(paste0("^\\s*", comp, " \\("), txt)[1]
  if (is.na(i)) return(NULL)
  k <- grep("Repeatability estimation overview", txt); k <- k[k > i][1]
  if (is.na(k)) return(NULL)
  hdr  <- strsplit(trimws(txt[k + 1]), "\\s+")[[1]]
  vals <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(strsplit(trimws(txt[k + 2]), "\\s+")[[1]]))
  if (length(hdr) != length(vals)) return(NULL)
  setNames(vals, hdr)
}
rpt_row <- function(r, label, n_obs, n_ind, n_rep) {
  v <- if (is.null(r)) NULL else rpt_parse(r, "MainID")
  g <- function(x, nm) if (!is.null(x) && nm %in% names(x)) unname(x[[nm]]) else NA_real_
  if (is.null(v) && !is.null(r)) { message("Could not read R for ", label); print(summary(r)) }
  data.frame(variable = label, n_obs = n_obs, n_males = n_ind, n_repeat_males = n_rep,
             R = g(v, "R"), SE = g(v, "SE"), lwr = g(v, "2.5%"), upr = g(v, "97.5%"),
             P_LRT = g(v, "LRT_P"), P_permut = g(v, "P_permut"))
}

# All within-individual pairs of samples
within_pairs <- function(d) {
  d %>% group_by(MainID) %>% filter(n() > 1) %>%
    group_modify(function(g, key) {
      ij <- t(combn(nrow(g), 2))
      data.frame(row_1 = g$row[ij[, 1]], row_2 = g$row[ij[, 2]],
                 trip_1 = g$trip[ij[, 1]], trip_2 = g$trip[ij[, 2]],
                 year_1 = g$year[ij[, 1]], year_2 = g$year[ij[, 2]])
    }) %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(lag_years = abs(year_2 - year_1))
}
```

```{r data}
males1 <- males %>% distinct(MainID, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

# 1. Are there discrete isotopic groups?

## Gaussian mixture models

δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N are strongly correlated, so models must allow correlated
(ellipsoidal) groups; models that assume uncorrelated isotopes can split one
elongated cloud into spurious groups. Models with 1–4 groups are compared by
BIC (higher is better in `mclust`); one group means no discrete structure.

```{r mixture}
Z1 <- scale(males1[ISO])
cor(males1$d13C, males1$d15N, method = "spearman")

bic1 <- mclust::mclustBIC(Z1, G = 1:4)
summary(bic1)
plot(bic1)

# Best model among those allowing correlated isotopes (full covariance)
full_models <- c("EEE", "VVV", "EEV", "VEV", "EVE", "VVE", "EVV", "VEE")
bic_full <- bic1[, intersect(full_models, colnames(bic1)), drop = FALSE]
best <- which(bic_full == max(bic_full, na.rm = TRUE), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
cat("Best correlated model:", colnames(bic_full)[best[2]], "with G =", rownames(bic_full)[best[1]], "\n")
round(bic_full, 1)

# Sensitivity: all samples
bic_all <- mclust::mclustBIC(scale(males[ISO]), G = 1:4)
summary(bic_all)
```

## Bootstrap likelihood-ratio test (1 vs 2 vs 3 groups)

```{r mixture-lrt}
set.seed(SEED)
lrt <- mclust::mclustBootstrapLRT(Z1, modelName = "VVV", nboot = N_BOOT_LRT, maxG = 2, verbose = FALSE)
lrt
```

## Null-model test of cluster structure

The silhouette of Ward + k-means clusters is compared with that obtained from
data simulated from a single bivariate normal distribution with the observed
means and covariance (one correlated cloud, no groups).

```{r null-structure}
mu <- colMeans(Z1); Sg <- cov(Z1)
set.seed(SEED)
null_struct <- do.call(rbind, lapply(2:4, function(k) {
  obs <- mean(silhouette(hcpc_lite(Z1, k), dist(Z1))[, 3])
  sim <- replicate(N_NULL, {
    Y <- MASS::mvrnorm(nrow(Z1), mu, Sg)
    mean(silhouette(hcpc_lite(Y, k), dist(Y))[, 3])
  })
  data.frame(k = k, silhouette = obs, null_median = median(sim),
             null_95 = quantile(sim, 0.95), p = (1 + sum(sim >= obs)) / (N_NULL + 1))
}))
rownames(null_struct) <- NULL
null_struct %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
write.csv(null_struct, file.path(OUT, "1_null_structure.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

**Interpretation.** Discrete groups are supported only if a correlated mixture
model with ≥ 2 groups clearly beats one group (ΔBIC > 6), the bootstrap LRT
rejects one group, and the silhouette exceeds the null. Otherwise, describe
male isotopes as a continuum (Section 2).

# 2. The isotopic gradient

The first principal component of the standardised isotopes summarises the main
axis of variation; positive scores = higher δ¹³C (and δ¹⁵N), i.e. more coastal /
continental-margin values; negative = more oceanic.

```{r gradient}
pca_iso <- prcomp(males[ISO], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
males$gradient <- pca_iso$x[, 1] * sign(cor(pca_iso$x[, 1], males$d13C))
summary(pca_iso)$importance[, 1]
round(pca_iso$rotation, 2)

if (requireNamespace("diptest", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(diptest::dip.test(males$gradient[!duplicated(males$MainID)]))
} else message("Install 'diptest' for a formal test of unimodality.")

g <- ggplot(males %>% distinct(MainID, .keep_all = TRUE), aes(gradient)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = "#d73027", colour = "white") + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Isotopic gradient score (PC1; + = higher δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N)",
       y = "Number of males")
g
ggsave(file.path(FIG, "2_gradient_distribution.pdf"), g, width = 7, height = 4, device = cairo_pdf)
write.csv(males, file.path(OUT, "2_males_with_gradient.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# 3. What explains isotopic position?

One sample per male (earliest with length data). Each term is tested with
Freedman–Lane permutation tests adjusting for the others.

```{r explain}
ml <- males %>% filter(!is.na(length_cm)) %>% distinct(MainID, .keep_all = TRUE)
cat(nrow(ml), "males with standard length\n")
set.seed(SEED)
expl <- bind_rows(lapply(c(ISO, "gradient"), function(v) bind_rows(
  fl_test(ml, v, "length_cm", c("Trip", "Year")),
  fl_test(ml, v, "Trip",      c("length_cm", "Year")),
  fl_test(ml, v, "Year",      c("length_cm", "Trip")))))
expl$p_BH <- p.adjust(expl$p_perm, "BH")
expl %>% mutate(across(c(F, p_perm, p_BH), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
write.csv(expl, file.path(OUT, "3_explanatory_tests.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Slopes per 10 cm of length
sapply(setNames(ISO, ISO), function(v) {
  f <- lm(reformulate(c("length_cm", "Trip", "Year"), v), data = ml)
  round(c(slope_per_10cm = 10 * coef(f)[["length_cm"]], 10 * confint(f)["length_cm", ]), 3)
})

g <- ml %>% pivot_longer(all_of(ISO), names_to = "isotope") %>%
  ggplot(aes(length_cm, value)) + geom_point(aes(shape = trip), size = 2.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~ isotope, scales = "free_y") + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Standard length (cm)", y = "‰", shape = "Trip")
g
ggsave(file.path(FIG, "3_isotopes_vs_length.pdf"), g, width = 8, height = 4, device = cairo_pdf)
```

# 4. Isotopic niche: males vs female strategies

Males (one sample per male) are compared with each female strategy
(Post-Breeding strategies; Post-Moult females as one group, since they form a
continuum). None of these groups were defined from isotopes, so differences
are not circular.

```{r niche-data}
niche_dat <- bind_rows(
  males1 %>% transmute(group = "Males", year, d13C, d15N),
  females %>% transmute(group, year, d13C, d15N)) %>%
  group_by(group) %>% filter(n() >= MIN_GROUP_N) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, intersect(names(GROUP_COLS), unique(group))))
table(niche_dat$group)

# Mean differences: males vs each female group (Welch t-tests, BH-adjusted)
mdiff <- bind_rows(lapply(setdiff(levels(niche_dat$group), "Males"), function(gr) bind_rows(lapply(ISO, function(v) {
  tt <- t.test(niche_dat[[v]][niche_dat$group == "Males"], niche_dat[[v]][niche_dat$group == gr])
  data.frame(comparison = paste("Males -", gr), isotope = v,
             difference = unname(diff(rev(tt$estimate))), lwr = tt$conf.int[1], upr = tt$conf.int[2],
             p = tt$p.value)
}))))
mdiff$p_BH <- p.adjust(mdiff$p, "BH")
mdiff %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
write.csv(mdiff, file.path(OUT, "4_male_female_differences.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## nicheROVER: niche size and directional overlap

```{r nicherover}
run_niche <- function(d, nsamples = N_POST) {
  d$group <- droplevels(d$group)
  set.seed(SEED)
  par <- tapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), d$group,
                function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = nsamples, X = as.matrix(d[ii, ISO])))
  seab <- sapply(par, function(sp) apply(sp$Sigma, 3, function(S) pi * sqrt(det(S))))
  nr95 <- sapply(par, function(sp) apply(sp$Sigma, 3, niche.size, alpha = 0.95))
  set.seed(SEED)
  ov <- overlap(par, nreps = nsamples, nprob = nsamples, alpha = c(0.95, 0.99))
  list(par = par, seab = seab, nr95 = nr95, overlap = ov)
}
nb <- run_niche(niche_dat)
lev <- colnames(nb$seab)
sea_c <- tapply(seq_len(nrow(niche_dat)), niche_dat$group, function(ii) {
  m <- length(ii); pi * sqrt(det(cov(niche_dat[ii, ISO]))) * (m - 1) / (m - 2) })
size_tab <- data.frame(group = lev, n = as.vector(table(niche_dat$group)[lev]),
  SEAc = as.vector(sea_c[lev]),
  SEAb_median = apply(nb$seab, 2, median),
  SEAb_lwr = apply(nb$seab, 2, quantile, 0.025), SEAb_upr = apply(nb$seab, 2, quantile, 0.975),
  NR95_median = apply(nb$nr95, 2, median))
size_tab %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
write.csv(size_tab, file.path(OUT, "4_niche_size.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# P(male niche larger than each female group's)
round(sapply(setdiff(lev, "Males"), function(gr) mean(nb$seab[, "Males"] > nb$seab[, gr])), 3)

# Directional overlap (%): P(an individual of the row group falls in the column group's 95% niche)
ov_mean <- apply(nb$overlap, c(1:2, 4), mean) * 100
ov_ci   <- apply(nb$overlap * 100, c(1:2, 4), quantile, prob = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)
round(ov_mean[, , 1], 1)
ov_long <- expand.grid(from = lev, into = lev, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  filter(from != into, from == "Males" | into == "Males") %>%
  mutate(mean = mapply(function(a, b) ov_mean[a, b, 1], from, into),
         lwr  = mapply(function(a, b) ov_ci[1, a, b, 1], from, into),
         upr  = mapply(function(a, b) ov_ci[2, a, b, 1], from, into))
ov_long %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 1)))
write.csv(ov_long, file.path(OUT, "4_niche_overlap_95.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r niche-plots, fig.height = 6}
cols <- unname(GROUP_COLS[lev])
set.seed(SEED)
par50 <- tapply(seq_len(nrow(niche_dat)), niche_dat$group,
                function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = 50, X = as.matrix(niche_dat[ii, ISO])))
dl <- tapply(seq_len(nrow(niche_dat)), niche_dat$group, function(ii) as.matrix(niche_dat[ii, ISO]))
niche.plot(niche.par = par50, niche.data = dl, pfrac = 0.05,
           iso.names = expression(delta^{13}*C, delta^{15}*N), col = cols)

g <- ggplot(niche_dat, aes(d13C, d15N, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.8) +
  stat_ellipse(level = 0.40, type = "norm", linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = GROUP_COLS, name = NULL) + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "δ¹³C (‰)", y = "δ¹⁵N (‰)",
       caption = "Ellipses: 40% (standard ellipse)")
g
ggsave(file.path(FIG, "4_niche_ellipses.pdf"), g, width = 8, height = 5, device = cairo_pdf)
```

## SIBER: standard ellipse areas and ellipse overlap

```{r siber, eval = HAS_SIBER}
codes <- setNames(paste0("G", seq_along(lev)), lev)
siber <- SIBER::createSiberObject(data.frame(iso1 = niche_dat$d13C, iso2 = niche_dat$d15N,
                                             group = unname(codes[as.character(niche_dat$group)]),
                                             community = 1))
ell_id <- setNames(paste0("1.", codes), lev)
ml_siber <- SIBER::groupMetricsML(siber); colnames(ml_siber) <- lev[match(colnames(ml_siber), ell_id)]
round(ml_siber, 3)
set.seed(SEED)
ell_post <- SIBER::siberMVN(siber, SIBER_PARMS, SIBER_PRIORS)
sea_b <- SIBER::siberEllipses(ell_post); colnames(sea_b) <- lev[match(names(ell_post), ell_id)]
siber_size <- data.frame(group = colnames(sea_b), SEAc = ml_siber["SEAc", colnames(sea_b)],
                         SEAb_median = apply(sea_b, 2, median),
                         SEAb_lwr = apply(sea_b, 2, quantile, 0.025),
                         SEAb_upr = apply(sea_b, 2, quantile, 0.975), row.names = NULL)
siber_size %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
write.csv(siber_size, file.path(OUT, "4_SIBER_niche_size.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

q3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
                          quantile(x, .025, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(x, .975, na.rm = TRUE))
set.seed(SEED)
siber_ov <- bind_rows(lapply(setdiff(lev, "Males"), function(gr) {
  b <- SIBER::bayesianOverlap(ell_id[["Males"]], ell_id[[gr]], ell_post,
                              draws = SIBER_DRAWS, p.interval = SIBER_P, n = 100)
  data.frame(comparison = paste("Males vs", gr),
             prop_of_union = q3(b$overlap / (b$area1 + b$area2 - b$overlap)),
             prop_of_male_ellipse = q3(b$overlap / b$area1),
             prop_of_female_ellipse = q3(b$overlap / b$area2))
}))
siber_ov
write.csv(siber_ov, file.path(OUT, "4_SIBER_overlap.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Sensitivity: females from the same years as males

Males were sampled only in `r paste(range(males$year), collapse = "–")`.
Isotopic baselines vary among years, so the comparison is repeated with females
from the same years only (groups with fewer than `MIN_GROUP_N` females are dropped).

```{r niche-sameyears}
yrs <- unique(males$year)
nd_y <- bind_rows(
  males1 %>% transmute(group = "Males", year, d13C, d15N),
  females %>% filter(year %in% yrs) %>% transmute(group, year, d13C, d15N)) %>%
  group_by(group) %>% filter(n() >= MIN_GROUP_N) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, intersect(names(GROUP_COLS), unique(group))))
table(nd_y$group)

# Male - female differences adjusted for year
set.seed(SEED)
bind_rows(lapply(setdiff(levels(nd_y$group), "Males"), function(gr) bind_rows(lapply(ISO, function(v) {
  d <- nd_y %>% filter(group %in% c("Males", gr)) %>%
    mutate(group = relevel(droplevels(group), "Males"), Year = factor(year))
  f <- lm(reformulate(c("group", "Year"), v), data = d)
  cf <- coef(f)[2]; ci <- confint(f)[2, ]
  data.frame(comparison = paste("Males -", gr), isotope = v,
             difference = -unname(cf), lwr = -unname(ci[2]), upr = -unname(ci[1]),
             p_perm = fl_test(d, v, "group", "Year", B = 4999)$p_perm)
})))) %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 3)))

nb_y <- run_niche(nd_y, nsamples = 5000)
round(apply(nb_y$overlap, c(1:2, 4), mean)[, , 1] * 100, 1)
round(apply(nb_y$seab, 2, median), 3)
```

# 5. Repeatability

## Population-level repeatability

All males are used (males sampled once help estimate the variance
components). Year is a fixed effect, because three years are too few for a
random effect. With only `r sum(table(males$MainID) > 1)` repeat males, the
estimates are exploratory and CIs will be wide.

```{r rpt}
rep_ids <- names(which(table(males$MainID) > 1))
set.seed(SEED)
rpt_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(ISO, function(v) {
  d_rep <- males %>% filter(MainID %in% rep_ids) %>% mutate(MainID = factor(MainID))
  d_all <- males %>% mutate(MainID = factor(MainID))
  ra <- tryCatch(fit_rpt(reformulate(c("Trip", "(1 | MainID)"), v), grname = "MainID", data = d_rep,
                         datatype = "Gaussian", nboot = N_RPT_BOOT, npermut = N_RPT_PERM),
                 error = function(e) NULL)
  rb <- tryCatch(fit_rpt(reformulate(c("Trip", "Year", "(1 | MainID)"), v), grname = "MainID", data = d_all,
                         datatype = "Gaussian", nboot = N_RPT_BOOT, npermut = N_RPT_PERM),
                 error = function(e) NULL)
  bind_rows(
    rpt_row(ra, paste(v, "(a) original: repeat males, trip"), nrow(d_rep), length(rep_ids), length(rep_ids)),
    rpt_row(rb, paste(v, "(b) all males, trip + year"), nrow(d_all), nlevels(d_all$MainID), length(rep_ids)))
}))
rpt_tab %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
write.csv(rpt_tab, file.path(OUT, "5_repeatability.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Within-male differences vs males sampled in the same years

```{r rpt-pairs}
pr <- within_pairs(males %>% dplyr::select(MainID, row, trip, year)) %>%
  mutate(abs_d13C = abs(males$d13C[row_1] - males$d13C[row_2]),
         abs_d15N = abs(males$d15N[row_1] - males$d15N[row_2]),
         abs_gradient = abs(males$gradient[row_1] - males$gradient[row_2]))
pr %>% dplyr::select(MainID, trip_1, year_1, trip_2, year_2, abs_d13C, abs_d15N) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2)))

cands <- function(male, tp, yr) {
  c1 <- which(males$MainID != male & males$trip == tp & males$year == yr)
  if (length(c1)) c1 else which(males$MainID != male & males$trip == tp)
}
c1 <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(pr)), function(k) cands(pr$MainID[k], pr$trip_1[k], pr$year_1[k]))
c2 <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(pr)), function(k) cands(pr$MainID[k], pr$trip_2[k], pr$year_2[k]))
set.seed(SEED)
null_d <- replicate(N_PERM, {
  d <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pr)), function(k) {
    a <- pick1(c1[[k]]); bc <- c2[[k]][males$MainID[c2[[k]]] != males$MainID[a]]
    if (!length(bc)) return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_))
    b <- pick1(bc)
    c(abs(males$d13C[a] - males$d13C[b]), abs(males$d15N[a] - males$d15N[b]),
      abs(males$gradient[a] - males$gradient[b]))
  }, numeric(3))
  rowMeans(d, na.rm = TRUE)
})
obs_d <- c(mean(pr$abs_d13C), mean(pr$abs_d15N), mean(pr$abs_gradient))
pair_tab <- data.frame(measure = c("d13C", "d15N", "gradient score"), n_pairs = nrow(pr),
                       mean_abs_diff_same_male = obs_d, mean_abs_diff_year_matched = rowMeans(null_d),
                       P = (1 + rowSums(null_d <= obs_d)) / (N_PERM + 1))
pair_tab %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
write.csv(pair_tab, file.path(OUT, "5_within_male_differences.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Suggested Methods text

*Males were sampled for stable isotopes (δ¹³C, δ¹⁵N) on arrival at the colony
(2011–2013; n samples, n males) and measured for standard length; no tracking
data were available. We tested for discrete isotopic groups with Gaussian
mixture models allowing correlated isotopes (1–4 components; mclust), a
parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio test of one vs two components, and by
comparing the silhouette width of Ward clusters with that obtained from data
simulated from a single bivariate normal distribution. Because these tests did
not support discrete groups [update from results], we summarised isotopic
variation as each male's score on the first principal component of the
standardised isotopes, and tested whether it varied with standard length, trip
type and year (Freedman–Lane permutation tests, one sample per male). Male
isotopic niche size (SEAc, SEA_B) and directional overlap with each female
strategy were estimated with SIBER and nicheROVER (default non-informative
prior), including a sensitivity analysis restricted to females sampled in the
same years. Repeatability of isotope values was estimated with linear mixed
models (trip type and year as fixed effects, individual as random effect;
rptR), and within-male differences were compared with those between males
sampled in the same years and trip types (9,999 randomisations).*
